What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0115-0006 at 14:30 on 2022-11-24 found crude oil on the pad: about 2.0% of the pad area, estimated 1.0 bbl. The inspector noted: "Oil sheen around cellar." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 2.9 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to the flanged flowline connection at the wellhead cellar.

Root cause

A failed gasket on the flange where the flowline leaves the wellhead.

Safety and permits

  3. Fitted a new gasket and new bolts, torqued to specification.
  4. Excavated the stained soil around the cellar.

Summary of the fix: replaced the flange gasket and bolts and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Maintenance Report — MNT-0115-020

What happened

Field staff reported that the operator noticed the pump jack running unusually light and no fluid reaching the flowline. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0115-0129 showed the wellhead at 21.0 °C with the air at 18.1 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A dynamometer card showed no load from the downhole pump, which points to a parted rod. The company workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 9 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

Fatigue failure of a rod body, probably started by corrosion pitting.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rod string and located the break.
  3. Recovered the lower section with an overshot fishing tool.
  4. Replaced the damaged rods.
  5. Ran the rod string back in and spaced out the pump.

Summary of the fix: fished and replaced parted rod section.

Testing and return to service

Maintenance Report — MNT-0115-029

Asset: WELL-0115 (NE-07 Well 115, T200, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: flowline Work started: 07 Nov 2025 08:00 · Finished: 07 Nov 2025 18:00 · Well stopped for this job: 10 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Kevin Price · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0115-0159 on 2025-11-06 Report written: 08 Nov 2025

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0115-0159 at 08:45 on 2025-11-06 found crude oil on the pad: about 1.9% of the pad area, estimated 0.4 bbl. The inspector noted: "Pooled fluid near flowline." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 8.7 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Corrosion under a failed protective wrap on the coupling. This is corrective repair number 3 on this well's flowline in the last 12 months.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 3 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 3% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 220 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 176 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 0.7 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0115-029 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.46% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0115-034

Asset: WELL-0115 (NE-07 Well 115, T200, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 26 Jun 2026 08:00 · Finished: 30 Jun 2026 08:00 · Well stopped for this job: 96 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Kevin Price · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0115-0192 on 2026-06-25 Report written: 01 Jul 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that the motor breaker kept tripping and the pump jack would not run. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0115-0192 showed the wellhead at 38.6 °C with the air at 33.7 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 2 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Root cause

Moisture got into the motor terminal box and damaged the windings.

Safety and permits

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.
